classFeature.name: Dragon Statistics
entries: The dragon has abilities and game statistics determined in part by their level. As shown below:
{@b Hit Die:} {@dice 1d4}(Tiny), {@dice 1d6}(Small), {@dice 1d8}(Medium), {@dice 1d10}(Large), {@dice 1d12}(Huge).
{@b Armor Class:} 11 + Constitution modifier + Proficiency bonus.
{@b Speed:} 20 feet (Tiny), 30 feet (Small), 35 feet (Large), 45 feet (Huge). Same for Swim Speed.
{@b Languages:} {@language Common}, {@language Draconic}.
{@b Immunity:} Dragon Ancestry Damage Type.
{@b Senses:} Darkvision (60 feet).
{@b Size:} Tiny (1st level), Small (4th level), Medium (8th level), Large (13th level), Huge (18th level).

classFeature.name: Dragon's Size
entries: The dragon’s size determines what actions they can take, some of their statistics and the power of their attacks. At 1st level, the dragon is considered Tiny and can't yet take the {@action Attack} action. They increase in size to Small at 4th level, Medium at 8th level, Large at 13th level and Huge at 18th level.

classFeature.name: Dragon's Flight
entries: At 1st level, while Tiny, the dragon has yet to master flying. The dragon learns how to fly once they are considered Small size, at a speed equal to half their Movement Speed. Their Fly Speed increases to match their full Movement Speed when the dragon reaches Medium size. Finally, at Large size, the dragon can fly at a speed equal to twice their Movement speed.

While Medium, and with a saddle, the dragon can carry, normally, up to one Medium sized creature on their back. In case they’re carrying two Medium sized creatures, their Flight Speed is halved and they gain a point of exhaustion for each hour of flight.

When they’re considered Large, and with a bigger saddle, the dragon can normally carry up to four Medium sized creatures, or a Large one, on their back. In case they’re carrying five Medium sized creatures, their Flight Speed is halved and they gain a point of exhaustion for each hour of flight.

Finally, when they’re considered Huge, and with an even bigger saddle, the dragon can normally carry up to nine Medium sized creatures, or two Large ones. If they’re carrying ten to twelve Medium sized creatures, or three Large ones, their Flight Speed is Halved and they gain a point of exhaustion for each hour of flight.

classFeature.name: Dragon's Food
entries: The dragon can only eat fresh meat, cooked or raw, and their size influences how much food per day they need to eat to be satiated. The following table informs the amount of food they must consume per day, compared to an adult person, according to their size.

entries.caption: Dragon Food Needed for each Dragon Size
colLabels: Amount of Food Needed (Compared to an Adult Person)

entries: Alternatively, once they reach Medium size, the dragon can fly freely on their surroundings to hunt their own food. To gather enough food this way, the dragon must spend 2 hours in a day hunting.

classFeature.name: Dragon Ancestry
entries: The dragon’s ancestry defines the damage type of their abilities and their rider’s. Furthermore, it is related to the Ability Score that represents their Connection to their ancestors and their rider. They can choose an option for both according to the Dragon Ancestry Damage Type and Dragon Ancestry Ability Score tables.

classFeature.name: Draconic Bond
entries: At 3rd level you choose what kind of bond the dragon have with heir rider. Your choice determines their interactions and grants features at 3rd level and again at 4th, 8th, 13th and 18th level.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When the dragon reaches 4th level, they can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or they can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, they can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a {@5etools feat|feats.html}.

classFeature.name: Draconic Bond feature
entries: At 4th level, the dragon gains a feature granted by their Draconic Bond.

classFeature.name: Breath Weapon
entries: Starting at 6th level, the dragon has developed the ability to unleash raw, destructive energy from their mouth.

As an action on their turn, the dragon can exhale destructive energy. Each creature in a 15-foot cone in front of them must make a Dexterity saving throw against their Breat Weapon save DC. Each creature takes {@dice 2d10} damage of their Dragon Ancestry Damage Type on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. {@b The dragon’s Breath Weapon save DC = 8 + the dragon’s Constitution modifier + Proficiency Bonus.}

The dragon can use this trait a number of times equal to their Constitution modifier, and they regain all expended uses when they finish a long rest. The area of effect and the damage of the breath weapon increase with their size.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When the dragon reaches 8th level, they can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or they can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, they can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

classFeature.name: Draconic Bond feature
entries: At 8th level, the dragon gains a feature granted by their Draconic Bond.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: When the dragon reaches 12th level, they can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or they can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, they can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

classFeature.name: Draconic Bond feature
entries: At 13th level, the dragon gains a feature granted by their Draconic Bond.

classFeature.name: Titanic Roar
entries: Starting at 13th level, the dragon can let loose a vicious roar, filling nearby creatures with dread.

As an action on their turn, the dragon can roar. Any number of creatures of your choice within 30 feet of the dragon must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Breath Weapon DC. On a failed save, creatures are {@condition frightened} of the dragon for 1 minute. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end each of their turns, ending the effect on a success.
Once the dragon has used this ability, they can't do so again until they finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Ancestral Magic
entries: The practitioner of Ancestral Magic channels the primeval arcane energies that seep from their dragon’s lineage into their own soul. By manifesting a magical Ancestral Weapon, these riders weave martial strikes with ancestral power, allowing them to replace traditional weapon attacks with rays of energy, protective shields, or chained strikes that lash out at multiple foes. This bond enables a rider to harmonize their magic with their companion’s nature, altering the elemental damage of their spells to match their dragon’s ancestry while extending the reach of their magic to protect or empower their companion. As their connection matures, the rider and dragon become a single conduit for ancient forces, culminating in a state where the rider fully embodies their dragon’s ancestral form to dominate the battlefield.

subclassFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: At 3rd level, the dragon's rider have learned to channel their dragon’s ancestral arcane magic that seeps through them. They may change the damage type of any spell that deals damage to that of their Dragon Ancestry Damage Type. Furthermore, the rider can make any spell they cast that targets only them to also target their dragon, if they’re within 30 feet of them. They can cast a spell this way a number of times equal to the dragon’s Dragon Ancestry Ability Score modifier and they regain all expended uses when they finish a long rest.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: The dragon's rider learns cantrips of your choice from the Ancestral spell list as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Rider’s Ancestral Spellcasting table.

Additionally, as a bonus action on their turn, they can command their dragon to use their action to cast an Ancestral cantrip they know on their next turn. They use their Dragon Ancestry Ability Score modifier as their spellcasting ability for these spells and, if that spell deals damage, they may change its damage type to that of their Dragon Ancestry Damage Type.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Ancestral Magic Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots the dragon's rider have to cast their Ancestral spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these Ancestral spells, they must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. They regain all expended spell slots when they finish a long rest.

entries.name: Spells Known
entries: The Spells Known column of the Ancestral Magic Spellcasting table shows how many Ancestral spells the dragon's rider know at a given level and when they learn more Ancestral spells of your choice. Each of these spells must be chosen from the Ancestral spells list and be of a level for which they have spell slots.

Additionally, whenever they gain a level, they can choose any of the Ancestral spells they know and replace it with another spell from the Ancestral spells list, which also must be of a level for which they have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: The dragon's spellcasting ability for their Ancestral spells is defined by their Dragon Ancestry, since the power of their magic relies on their connection to their ancestors. They use their Dragon Ancestry Ability Score whenever a spell refers to their spellcasting ability. In addition, they use their Dragon Ancestry Ability Score modifier when setting the saving throw DC for an Ancestral spell they cast and when making an attack roll with one.

subclassFeature.name: Small Dragon
entries: At 4th level the dragon grows and is considered Small in size. They are now ready for battle and, as a bonus action on the rider's turn, they can command their dragon to take the {@action Attack} action. If they do so, on the dragon's next turn, they can use their action to take the {@action Attack} action and make a Claw attack. The damage of their attacks are considered magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

Alternatively, they can choose to use their Bite attack. The dragon can attack this way a number of times equal to their Strength modifier (minimum of once.) They regain all expended uses when they finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Claw Attack Small
entries: The dragon strikes with their claws at a target within 5 feet.

{@b Claw attack.} {@i Melee Weapon Attack:} (Strength score modifier + Proficiency bonus) to hit, reach 5ft., one target. On a hit the target takes {@dice 1d4} + Strength score modifier slashing damage.

subclassFeature.name: Bite Attack Small
entries: The dragon bites viciously at a target within 5 feet.

{@b Bite attack.} {@i Melee Weapon Attack:} (Strength score modifier + Proficiency bonus) to hit, reach 5ft., one target. On a hit the target takes {@dice 1d4} + Strength score modifier piercing damage plus {@dice 1d6} damage of their Dragon Ancestry Damage Type.

subclassFeature.name: Medium Dragon
entries: At 8th level the dragon grows and is considered Medium in size. At Medium size, the dragon gains two other attack options that they can choose to use instead of their Bite attack: a Tail attack or a Wing Attack.

subclassFeature.name: Claw Attack Medium
entries: The dragon slashes with their claws at a target within 5 feet.

{@b Claw attack.} {@i Melee Weapon Attack:} (Strength score modifier + Proficiency bonus) to hit, reach 5ft., one target. On a hit the target takes {@dice 2d4} + Strength score modifier slashing damage.

subclassFeature.name: Tail Attack Medium
entries: The dragon strikes a distant foe with their tail.

{@b Tail attack.} {@i Melee Weapon Attack:} (Strength score modifier + Proficiency bonus) to hit, reach 10tf., one target. On a hit the target takes {@dice 2d4} + Strength score modifier bludgeoning damage, and must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be knocked {@condition prone} {@b (DC = 8 + their proficiency bonus + the dragon's Strength modifier)}.

subclassFeature.name: Wing Attack Medium
entries: The dragon beats their wings, bashing enemies around them.

{@b Wing attack.} Rather than making an attack, the dragon can beat their wings. Creatures of your choice within 10 feet of the dragon must make a Strength saving throw {@b (DC = 8 + the dragon's proficiency bonus + the dragon's Strength modifier)}. On a failed save, a creature is pushed 10 feet away from the dragon. Immediately after making this special attack, the dragon can move up to half their flying speed.
